Squirrel gripper · simulation study

Cross-section, joint length & lateral bending: what the sim now supports, and what it says

Implemented the weekend experiment list in the finger simulation and ran controlled studies to fix parameters for the first Northeastern print iteration.

PyElastica Cosserat rod E = 20 MPa · L = 0.20 m 3 joints @ 7.6 / 11.6 / 16 cm Set 1 stiffness 2026-07-12

Bottom line: a wider rectangular finger is dramatically stiffer sideways with only a mild cost to curl — so width is the right knob for Lindsay's lateral-flop problem. Joint length and stiffness are now separate, controllable parameters, and the curl sim — which used to whip and collapse — is stable.

01What changed in the simulation

Three new finger.py flags, each defaulting to the old behavior so existing runs are unaffected.

CapabilityNew flagWhat it doesStatus
Per-joint length
(trapezoidal + longer joints)		 --joint_lengths Per-joint softened-region length in cm (e.g. 2.4,1.6,0.8). Shrinks toward the tip = "trapezoidal". Ready
Rectangular cross-section --cross_section rect Replaces the circular section; rescales bending/shear/mass to the true rectangle. Ready
Finger width & thickness --base_width
--base_thickness		 Width = lateral (y) dimension, thickness = curl (z) dimension. Decouples the two bending axes. Ready
Lateral bending measurement cantilever harness The contact sim is x–z only, so lateral bending is measured in a dedicated cantilever test. Ready

The rod frame sets the physics: curl bends about the width axis (resisted by I₂ ∝ w·t³) while sideways bending bends about the thickness axis (resisted by I₁ ∝ t·w³). That cubic on width is why widening the finger is such a strong lever on lateral stiffness.

02Finger width & shape — on the real jointed finger

Lindsay saw the printed finger flop sideways. The goal is a finger with soft joints that still curls but doesn't flop. So these are all run on the actual 3-joint finger with Set 1 soft joints — the same finger that grasps — not an idealized bar. Two questions: does a wider finger still curl, and does it flop less?

A · Does a wider finger still curl? Yes — rectangles keep curling.

B · Does width fix the sideways flop? Yes — even with the soft joints.

Jointed finger (Set 1)Sideways flopLateral stiffnessCurl angle
Circle ⌀20.5 mm2.01 mm9.9 N/m92°
Rect 25×18 mm1.01 mm19.8 N/m75°
Rect 30×18 mm0.64 mm31.0 N/m71°
Conclusion — width & shape: a wide-thin rectangle (25–30 × 18 mm) wins on both axes at once: it still curls like the circle (71° vs 92°) while flopping 2–3× less sideways, all with the same soft joints. Widen to fix the flop; keep thickness at 18 mm to preserve curl.
Why it works — the underlying cross-section physics (idealized uniform bar)

On a jointless uniform bar, the geometry is clean: a circle or square is isotropic (equal stiffness every direction, at any size), while a wide-thin rectangle is anisotropic — lateral stiffness grows ∝ width³, curl only ∝ width. That's the mechanism the jointed results above inherit.

03Stability fix — the fingers were collapsing

The earlier curl runs whipped and diverged. The cause was near-zero internal damping; raising it (plus contact damping and a longer settle time) makes every run stable.

The finger used AnalyticalLinearDamper with damping = 0.1, which dissipates only ~18% of velocity over a 2 s run — the finger was essentially undamped, so contact energy piled up and it whipped until coordinates blew past several meters. The fix has three parts, and your intuition about simulating longer was right: the curl is an over-damped approach to equilibrium, so with more damping it needs more time to fully curl.

ParameterBeforeAfter (stable)Why
Internal damping0.11.0dissipates whipping; keeps curl
Contact damping nu530absorbs penalty-contact energy
Contact vel-damp1090kills post-contact bounce
Contact stiffness k12504000less penetration into the branch
Sim time2.0 s5.0 sover-damped curl needs longer to settle

Result: all six study runs stay bounded for the full 150 frames (max coordinate ~0.15 m) and settle into a clean drape. Every curl result and animation below uses these stable settings.

04Joint length in the stable curl sim

Circular finger, 0.20 m, Set 1 joints, stable settings — varying joint length only.

ConfigPeak contactsWrap depthReading
Baseline — uniform 1.6 cm3−24 mmgentle drape
Longer — uniform 2.0 cm5−52 mmwraps deeper
Trapezoidal 2.4 / 1.6 / 0.85−50 mmdeep wrap, tip stays controlled
Two configs that collapse — and why it matters. Pushing joints too soft makes the finger buckle instead of wrap: uniform 2.4 cm joints (all three long) fold back on themselves, and the very soft Set 8 stiffness collapses the same way. Both are stable numerically (bounded) but physically buckled. This is the case for trapezoidal + Set 1: keeping the tip stiffer prevents the collapse. It also confirms Set 1 (0.10 / 0.08 / 0.06 MPa) as the right first request.
Conclusion — joint length: longer ≈ trapezoidal > short for wrap depth (−52 ≈ −50 > −24 mm). Longer joints wrap deeper, and trapezoidal matches that depth without the buckling that uniform-long joints hit once they get too soft — so trapezoidal is the robust pick: it takes the deep-wrap benefit of long joints while keeping the tip stiff enough not to collapse. Net ranking: long ≈ trapezoid > short, with trapezoid the safest of the two deep-wrap options.

Design decisionTestedRanking / callWhy
Cross-section shapecircle vs square vs wide rect (jointed) wide-thin rectangle on the jointed finger, a wide rect flops far less than a circle yet still curls; a 30×30 square is isotropic (over-stiffens curl). Also prints without supports
Finger width (lateral y)18 – 30 mm (jointed finger) wider = far less flop, curl kept rect 30×18 flops 0.64 mm vs circle's 2.0 mm (3.1× less) while still curling 71° vs 92°; this is the flop fix
Thickness (curl z)fixed 18 mm keep 18 mm thickness governs curl (∝ thickness³); tune this — not width — if curl needs adjusting
Joint length1.6 / 2.0 / 2.4 cm / trapezoid long ≈ trapezoid > short longer wraps deeper (−52 ≈ −50 > −24 mm); trapezoid matches it without the buckle uniform-long hits → safest deep-wrap pick
Joint stiffnessSet 1 … Set 8 Set 1 (stiffest) softer sets over-soften and buckle instead of gripping; Set 1 gives a controlled wrap

07Recommended first-iteration parameters

What I'd send Northeastern, consolidating the sim values with these results:

Finger length0.20 m
Cross-sectionrectangular 25 × 18 mm (W×T)
Number of joints3
Joint centers7.6 / 11.6 / 16.0 cm
Joint lengths (trapezoidal)2.4 / 1.6 / 0.8 cm
Link (stiff) modulus20 MPa
Joint stiffness — Set 10.10 / 0.08 / 0.06 MPa
  • Width is the lateral-stiffness lever. 25×18 mm doubles sideways rigidity vs a square; go 30×18 mm if it still flops.
  • Thickness governs curl — keep it at 18 mm to stay near the current curl behavior, tune it (not width) if curl needs adjusting.
  • Set 1 for the joints — softer sets (Set 8) over-soften and buckle instead of gripping.
  • Trapezoidal = shorter joints toward the tip, now a single sim flag; easy to sweep this weekend.
Stable sim settings (for anyone re-running finger.py / the dataset runner): internal --damping 1.0, --nu_contact 30, --vel_damp_contact 90, --k_contact 4000, --final_time 5.0. These replace the old damping 0.1 / 2 s that caused the divergence. Note the 5 s settle is ~2.5× slower per run than the old 2 s.
Generated from finger.py (curl sim) and a validated PyElastica cantilever harness, squirrel conda env. Cross-section physics: I₁=t·w³/12 (lateral), I₂=w·t³/12 (curl). Cantilever validated to 98.5% of FL³/3EI. Numbers are from single deterministic runs.
